audit_notes: Critical check: in a conditioned room at 25 C, an inner PCM layer melting at 26 C holds the inner surface at ~26 C, so the heat flux to the room during melting is h_i*(26-25) = 8 W/m2 whatever arrives from outside; without PCM the west wall delivers ~8.4 W/m2. The steady model therefore shows only a small gain; the latent store merely absorbs the wall flux and must be discharged at night. In hot climates night air is often 28-32 C, so the PCM does not resolidify without mechanical cooling - then the daily heat gain is unchanged and only the peak is shifted. The 'camel coat' exterior insulation was not quantified by the candidate and is not included; any insulation benefit would be conventional. Capacity check: 0.015 m*900 kg/m3*0.3*150 kJ/kg = 0.61 MJ/m2, enough to absorb ~20 h of 8.4 W/m2, so capacity is not limiting - resolidification is. Dimensionless: Stefan number cp*dT/L = 2000*5/150000 = 0.067 (latent-dominated); Biot envelope 0.027. Simulation coefficient: effective inner clamp coupling 1000 W/m2K. Metric: heat flux to the room = h_i*(T(1) - T_indoor), via value_at x=1 with transform. Baseline: no PCM (clamp 0). Expected gain ~5% during melting hours only. Mechanical: PCM plaster fire class and capsule leakage over 20 years are concerns but not safety-critical. Audit passed with the caveat that the steady model overstates daily benefit whenever resolidification fails.
